[ASSISTANT_SAID] If you're getting an `ApplicationError: No executable found for solver 'cbc'` when running your Pyomo model in Google Colab, it's likely that the CBC solver is not installed or not properly configured on your system.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To install CBC in Google Colab, you can run the command: `!apt-get install -y -qq coinor-cbc`.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] After installing CBC, you may need to add the CBC executable to your system path by running: `import os; os.environ['PATH'] += ':/usr/bin'`.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] After running these commands, you should be able to use CBC as a solver in Pyomo by setting the `solver_name` argument to `'cbc'` when calling the `SolverFactory` function.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Provided a code example for using CBC as a solver in Pyomo.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Code example for using CBC as a solver in Pyomo:  
```python
from pyomo.environ import *

model = ConcreteModel()

model.x = Var(within=NonNegativeReals)
model.y = Var(within=NonNegativeReals)

model.c1 = Constraint(expr=model.x + model.y >= 1)

model.obj = Objective(expr=model.x + model.y)

solver = SolverFactory('cbc')
results = solver.solve(model)

print(results)
```
